info.title: Gateway admin catalog API
info.description: Provider catalog administration: read immutable catalog releases (releases, provider accounts, deployments with capabilities and prices, routes), create and activate releases, manage encrypted provider credentials, override prices per deployment and operation, discover the models each provider account lists, and compare the prices a release bills with prices published by the gateway's price sources. Discovery and price sync never change a release or price. Authenticated with a session cookie or an agent token (`Authorization: Bearer gwa_…`), which acts only in its agent's organization. Credentials are never part of a release; they are stored encrypted per adapter instance key and are write-only: no response ever contains secret material.

get.summary: Catalog releases, newest first
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque signed token from `next_page_token`; bound to the actor, resolved release, filters, and ordering.

post.summary: Store a new, inactive catalog release
post.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `catalog_release.created`. The release is sealed but not activated.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

409.description: `release_exists` (a release with the same digest exists; its id is in `detail`), `idempotency_conflict`, or `idempotency_in_progress`.

get.summary: Provider accounts of one release, by adapter instance key
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. Reads one release: `release_id`, else the active release. With no active release and no `release_id`, returns `release_id: null` and no items. A page token is bound to the resolved release, so activating a new release mid-pagination makes the old token fail with `page_token_query_mismatch`; restart from the first page. Credentials are never stored in the catalog; `adapter_instance_key` names the runtime adapter configuration.

parameters.name: release_id
parameters.description: Release to read. Defaults to the organization's active release. A release outside the organization is `not_found`.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque signed token from `next_page_token`; bound to the actor, resolved release, filters, and ordering.

get.summary: Deployments of one release, by name, with per-operation capability and price
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. Reads one release: `release_id`, else the active release. With no active release and no `release_id`, returns `release_id: null` and no items. A page token is bound to the resolved release, so activating a new release mid-pagination makes the old token fail with `page_token_query_mismatch`; restart from the first page.

parameters.name: release_id
parameters.description: Release to read. Defaults to the organization's active release. A release outside the organization is `not_found`.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque signed token from `next_page_token`; bound to the actor, resolved release, filters, and ordering.

get.summary: Routes of one release, by alias then operation
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. Reads one release: `release_id`, else the active release. With no active release and no `release_id`, returns `release_id: null` and no items. A page token is bound to the resolved release, so activating a new release mid-pagination makes the old token fail with `page_token_query_mismatch`; restart from the first page.

parameters.name: release_id
parameters.description: Release to read. Defaults to the organization's active release. A release outside the organization is `not_found`.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque signed token from `next_page_token`; bound to the actor, resolved release, filters, and ordering.

post.summary: Activate a release (also used for rollback)
post.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `catalog_release.activated`. The organization activation pointer is versioned; `If-Match` guards concurrent activations. An idempotent replay returns the recorded response. `gateway catalog apply` also advances the activation version when it switches the active release.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: `*` for any current version (including none), `"v0"` for none yet (create only), or the `ETag` of the current version.

404.description: `not_found`: the release does not exist in the organization.

409.description: `price_override_incompatible` (an unrevoked, unexpired price override sets a price the release's provider family does not report usage for; its id is in `detail`), `version_conflict` (stale `If-Match`), `idempotency_conflict`, or `idempotency_in_progress`.

get.summary: A release's catalog as a manifest
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. The starting point for a release that changes the catalog: edit the manifest and create a release from it. A release keeps no item order, so providers are sorted by `adapter_instance_key`, deployments by `name`, capabilities by `operation`, prices by deployment and operation, and routes by alias and operation. A release created from the manifest unchanged has the same catalog; its digest equals this release's only if this release was created in that order. Another organization's release, or an unknown one, is `not_found`.

get.summary: Provider credential metadata
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. Metadata only.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque signed token from `next_page_token`; bound to the actor, resolved release, filters, and ordering.

200.description: Page of credential metadata ordered by adapter instance key.

put.summary: Set or rotate a provider credential
put.description: Permission `credential_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `provider_credential.set` without secret material. Authorization is checked before the key is looked up, so callers without `credential_write` get 403 for every key. The secret is validated for the family the active release declares for the key, or, when the active release does not declare it, the newest release that does (so it can be staged before activation), sealed with AES-256-GCM bound to the organization, key, and family, and stored encrypted. At inference time a stored credential replaces the gateway's own credential for its adapter instance key and uses that key's configured endpoint. A key with no gateway configuration can use a stored credential only for `openai`, `anthropic`, and `gemini`. A credential that cannot be used (sealed for another family, or undecryptable) makes requests routed to the key fail as unavailable rather than fall back to the gateway's credential.

parameters.name: adapter_instance_key
parameters.description: Provider account key declared by a release of the organization.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: `*` for any current version (including none), `"v0"` for none yet (create only), or the `ETag` of the current version.

200.description: Rotated, or idempotent replay. A replay returns the response recorded by the original request, even if the credential has since been rotated or deleted, or an activation has changed the family its key resolves to.

404.description: `provider_account_not_found`: no release of the organization declares the key.

delete.description: Permission `credential_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `provider_credential.deleted`. Authorization is checked before the credential is looked up.

parameters.name: adapter_instance_key
parameters.description: Provider account key declared by a release of the organization.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: `*` for any current version (including none), `"v0"` for none yet (create only), or the `ETag` of the current version.

200.description: Idempotent replay of a completed delete.

404.description: `not_found`: no credential is stored for the key.

get.summary: Price overrides
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. Every override of the organization in any status, newest first.

parameters.name: deployment
parameters.description: Only overrides for this deployment name.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque signed token from `next_page_token`; bound to the actor, resolved release, filters, and ordering.

200.description: Page of overrides ordered by creation time, newest first.

post.summary: Override the price of a deployment and operation
post.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `price_override.created`. While effective (from `effective_from`, until `effective_until` if set, and not revoked), the override replaces the catalog price of every route to a deployment with this name and operation, in whichever release is active: reservations record its prices, currency and confidence, price source `override`, and price version `override:{id}`. When several overrides are effective, the one with the latest `effective_from` applies. At least one release of the organization must price the operation on a deployment of this name, and a price the family of any such release never reports usage for (cached input, reasoning, or other for `anthropic`; reasoning for `bedrock`) must be zero. Activating a release whose family cannot bill such a price is refused while the override is live. Overrides never apply retroactively: an `effective_from` in the past (by database time) starts now, and reservations already made keep their price.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

200.description: Idempotent replay: the response recorded by the original request.

422.description: `invalid_price_override` (invalid field, window, or a price the provider family never reports usage for), `unknown_deployment` (no release of the organization prices the operation on a deployment of this name), or `request_body_unprocessable` (unknown or mistyped fields).

post.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `price_override.revoked`. The override stops applying to new requests; reservations already priced by it keep that price and settle with it. Revocation is final.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The `ETag` of the override's current version, or `*`.

404.description: `not_found`: the override does not exist in the organization.

get.summary: Model discovery jobs
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. Every sync job of the organization, newest first. The worker lists each provider account of the active release every six hours; finished jobs are kept for 30 days, except each account's latest successful job.

parameters.name: adapter_instance_key
parameters.description: Only jobs for this adapter instance key.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque signed token from `next_page_token`; bound to the actor, filters, and ordering.

200.description: Page of sync jobs, newest first.

post.summary: Request model discovery for a provider account
post.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `catalog_sync_job.requested`. Queues a sync of one provider account of the active release; the worker runs it within about a minute. The listing is recorded as discovered models and never changes a release.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

200.description: Idempotent replay: the response recorded by the original request.

409.description: `catalog_sync_in_progress` (the account already has a queued or running job), `idempotency_conflict`, or `idempotency_in_progress`.

422.description: `unknown_provider_account` (the active release declares no provider account with this key, or the organization has no active release) or `request_body_unprocessable` (unknown or mistyped fields).

get.summary: Model discovery job
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited.

404.description: `not_found`: the job does not exist in the organization.

get.summary: Discovered models
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. Models the organization's provider accounts have listed, ordered by adapter instance key, family, and model. Capabilities and prices are not discovered. A model absent from a later successful listing is kept with `missing_since` for 90 days.

parameters.name: adapter_instance_key
parameters.description: Only models listed by this adapter instance key.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: `listed`: reported by the latest successful listing; `missing`: reported before but absent since.

parameters.name: deployed
parameters.description: Only models a deployment of the active release does (`true`) or does not (`false`) name on the same provider account.

parameters.name: evidence
parameters.description: Only models whose latest evidence (D-018) is in one of these states: a comma-separated set of `verified`, `refused`, `entitled`, `requires_action` and `none` (no evidence yet), such as `verified,entitled,none`.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque signed token from `next_page_token`; bound to the actor, filters, and ordering.

get.summary: Deployable models
get.description: Models the provider's catalog lets each provider account deploy (D-018): Azure's account model list, per format, model and version, refreshed by every successful listing of the account. Each lists the account's listed deployments serving it; one with none needs a deployment, which is the tenant's action (the gateway never creates deployments). Families without such a catalog have none. Requires `catalog_read`.

parameters.name: adapter_instance_key
parameters.description: Only models deployable on this adapter instance key.

parameters.name: deployed
parameters.description: Only models some listed deployment of the account serves (`true`) or none does (`false`).

parameters.name: lifecycle_status
parameters.description: Only models in this lifecycle status, compared without case (Azure: `GenerallyAvailable`, `Preview`, `Deprecating`, `Legacy`, `Deprecated`).

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque signed token from `next_page_token`; bound to the actor, filters, and ordering.

get.summary: Drift between the active release and discovered models
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. One entry per provider account of the active release. Drift fields are null until a listing of the account has succeeded.

404.description: `not_found`: the organization has no active release.

get.summary: Price sources
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. The gateway's configured price sources, ordered by `source`: operator price sheets configured with `GATEWAY_PRICE_SHEET_URL_{FAMILY}`, and the public price lists enabled with `GATEWAY_PUBLIC_PRICE_SOURCES`: the Azure Retail Prices API (`azure-retail:azure-openai`) and the AWS Price List (`aws-price-list:bedrock`), which keep on-demand token prices only. Sources are gateway-wide, not per organization; their URLs are never returned. A source no worker has configured for an hour is retired: no longer listed, fetched or compared. Configured again, it has no snapshot until a fetch succeeds. The worker fetches each daily, or within about a minute of a `catalog_write` request to fetch it now; after a failed fetch it retries 15 minutes later, then 30 minutes after that, and after a third consecutive failure waits for the next daily fetch.

post.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `price_source.fetch_requested`. Makes the source due now, so the worker fetches it within about a minute instead of at its next daily fetch, such as after opting an account into automatic offers. Sources are gateway-wide: a source attempted in the last 10 minutes, by any organization's request or the daily schedule, is not fetched again, and a request then answers `429`. The response is the source as it stands; read it again from the list to see the fetch's outcome.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Price source id, such as `price-sheet:openai` or `aws-price-list:bedrock`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

200.description: Idempotent replay: the response recorded by the original request.

404.description: `not_found`: no worker has a price source with this id configured.

429.description: `price_fetch_too_soon`: the source was attempted in the last 10 minutes, or is being fetched.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the source may be fetched again.

get.summary: Drift between the active release's prices and published prices
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. One entry per priced deployment operation of the active release, as billed now: an effective price override replaces the release's price. Each is compared with the current snapshot of every source of its provider family: the published price of the item the deployment is mapped to at that source (see price mappings), or else of the deployment's model; for the mapping's region if it pins one, else the deployment's `location` if there is one, else the global price; in the catalog price's currency only. Published decimals are converted to money units per token exactly; currencies are never converted. Nothing is applied: to adopt a published price, activate a release or create a price override.

404.description: `not_found`: the organization has no active release.

get.summary: Published prices
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. The prices in the current snapshot of every price source, ordered by source and then as published. Use it to find the item to map a deployment to.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only prices whose item or model contains this text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque signed token from `next_page_token`; bound to the actor, filters, and ordering.

400.description: `invalid_query` (unknown or invalid filter), or an invalid page size or token.

409.description: `page_token_stale`: the source the previous page ended in has published new prices since; start from the first page.

get.summary: Price mappings
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. The organization's price mappings, ordered by deployment and source.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque signed token from `next_page_token`; bound to the actor, filters, and ordering.

put.summary: Map a deployment to a published item
put.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `price_mapping.set`. Drift compares the deployment with this item's price at the source instead of matching its model. The deployment must be in the active release (or be the deployment an account's automatic offer would give a listed model, so a model that `needs_price` can be priced before it is offered) and the source live and of the deployment's provider family. A mapping names the deployment, so it outlives releases. Changes no price.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: `*` to create or replace, or the `ETag` of the mapping's current version.

422.description: `invalid_price_mapping` (invalid item or region), `unknown_deployment` (neither in the active release nor named by an automatic offer, or of another provider family), `unknown_price_source` (no live source of that name), or `request_body_unprocessable` (unknown or mistyped fields).

delete.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `price_mapping.deleted`. Drift goes back to matching the deployment's model.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The `ETag` of the mapping's current version, or `*`.

404.description: `not_found`: no mapping for the deployment at that source.

get.summary: What the organization's cloud accounts must name to trust the gateway
get.description: Permission `catalog_read` (owner, admin, operator, auditor, read-only member; org-wide only). Not audited. An AWS role a Bedrock credential names must require `aws_external_id` as `sts:ExternalId` in its trust policy: the gateway presents the organization's external ID, never one a credential supplies, so the role can be assumed only for this organization.

get.summary: Read an account's automatic model offer
get.description: Permission `catalog_read`. The opt-in, the latest run, and what it decided for each model the account's latest listing reports.

parameters.name: adapter_instance_key
parameters.description: The provider account's adapter instance key.

put.summary: Opt an account in to automatic model offers
put.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `catalog_auto_offer.set`. The account must be declared by the active release. Setting the opt-in queues a listing of the account (unless one is open). After each successful listing the worker offers every listed chat or embedding model a price source prices: a deployment named `{adapter_instance_key}-{model}` (characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]` become `-`; a model whose name another model's deployment already has gets the name cut short plus `-` and eight hex digits of the model identifier's SHA-256), its prices, and a route per operation whose alias is the model identifier (an alias already routing that operation keeps its route). A model is priced by the item its deployment is mapped to, otherwise by a price published for that exact model; public price lists name products rather than models, so their prices apply only through a mapping. An offered deployment's price then follows its source through automatic price adoption (`catalog/price-policy`), and offered deployments are removed when the listing no longer reports the model. Each change is a new release, created and activated by the system and audited as `catalog_release.created` and `catalog_release.activated`; the activation's version moves on, so a conditional activation made against the previous one is refused. Deployments an admin added are left alone, and an offered deployment that an admin's release dropped is `withdrawn` until the opt-in is set again. Saving the opt-in makes the active release the starting point, so models a rollback dropped are offered again; changing `location` moves offered deployments there.

parameters.name: adapter_instance_key
parameters.description: The provider account's adapter instance key.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: `*` for any state, or the `ETag` of the opt-in's current version.

422.description: `invalid_auto_offer` (invalid key or location), `unknown_provider_account` (not declared by the active release), or `request_body_unprocessable` (unknown or mistyped fields).

delete.summary: Opt an account out of automatic model offers
delete.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `catalog_auto_offer.deleted`. Deployments already offered stay in the catalog as they are and are no longer kept in step.

parameters.name: adapter_instance_key
parameters.description: The provider account's adapter instance key.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: `*` for any state, or the `ETag` of the opt-in's current version.

get.summary: Read whether prices follow their sources
get.description: Permission `catalog_read`. With `auto_adopt` (the default, also for an organization that never set it), after each price source fetch and at least hourly the worker adopts every published price that differs from the active release (D-024): matched by the deployment's price mapping or by its exact model, in the same currency, only the dimensions that differ, a price finer than one money unit rounded up. Prices billed through an override, and prices no source publishes, are left alone. Each change is a new release created and activated by the system and audited as `catalog_release.created`, `catalog_release.activated` and `catalog_release.prices_adopted`; the activation's version moves on, so a conditional activation made against the previous one is refused. A change that sets a billed dimension to zero, cuts one by more than half or more than doubles one, and a price two sources disagree about, is held instead (`/catalog/price-holds`). `version` is 0 until the policy is first set.

put.summary: Turn automatic price adoption on or off
put.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `catalog_price_policy.set`. Off, published prices are adopted only by hand (*Price changes*); on, the next run adopts what differs.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: `*` for any state, or the `ETag` of the policy's current version.

get.summary: Read the providers and locations requests may be sent to
get.description: Permission `catalog_read`. The organization's routing policy (D-023, Phase 9): the provider families and deployment locations its requests may be sent to. Route selection and failover consider only the deployments it permits, before weights apply; a request whose alias has no permitted deployment is refused with `403 routing_policy_denied` (batch lines with the same code), never sent somewhere else. `null` for a list permits any; a deployment with no `location` is not permitted while locations are restricted. A policy never set is returned with `version` 0, both lists `null`, and no `ETag`.

put.summary: Set the providers and locations requests may be sent to
put.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `routing_policy.set`. Replaces the whole policy: a list absent or `null` permits any. Lists are returned sorted, without duplicates. The change publishes a configuration version, so every gateway process routes by it once it loads that version (seconds; isolated data planes on their next poll). Requests already sent are not affected.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: `*` for any state, or the `ETag` of the policy's current version.

422.description: `invalid_routing_policy` (an empty list, more than 16 providers or 64 locations, an unknown provider family, or a location that is empty, longer than 255 characters, or has surrounding whitespace), or `request_body_unprocessable` (unknown or mistyped fields).

get.summary: List published prices held for an admin
get.description: Permission `catalog_read`. Open holds, newest first (at most 500); `all=true` includes resolved ones: `adopted` (the catalog now bills what was held, as when an admin adopted it under *Price changes*), `dismissed`, and `superseded` (the source or the catalog moved on). To adopt a held price, adopt it as any published price; the next run resolves the hold.

post.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Audited as `catalog_price_hold.dismissed`. The price is not adopted, and the same proposal (deployment, operation, source and proposed prices) is not held again until the source publishes something else.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: `*` for any state, or the `ETag` of the hold's current version.

get.summary: Models of a Bedrock account that need an agreement, with their offers
get.description: Permission `catalog_read`. Lists each foundation model whose evidence is `agreement_required` (its identifiers, the model and its inference profiles, collapsed to the foundation model whose AWS Marketplace agreement they need), and each model whose agreement was accepted through the gateway with where it stands. For a model still needing one, its live offers are read from Bedrock (`ListFoundationModelAgreementOffers`, `offerType=ALL`): offer id, rate card (the account's region's rates where the card names them, else the first 100), legal and support terms. Offer tokens are never returned. Reading offers needs the connection's optional *accept model agreements* permissions. Each model's offers are read on their own: one whose read is refused has `offers_error` `agreement_permission_missing`, and `permission` is `missing` only when every read was refused (`granted` when any succeeded). An agreement only removes the Marketplace requirement: AWS can still refuse a model it has not enabled for the account (see the operations guide, *Model access on your cloud account*). D-035.

parameters.name: adapter_instance_key
parameters.description: The Bedrock provider account's adapter instance key.

200.description: The account's models needing an agreement.

422.description: `invalid_agreement_request` (invalid key or body), `unknown_provider_account` (not declared by the active release), `agreements_unsupported` (the account is not Bedrock's), `agreements_need_tenant_credential` (the account is called with the gateway's process credential, not the organization's own: connect the account's role first).

502.description: `provider_unavailable`: Bedrock failed to list the account's models.

503.description: `agreements_unavailable` (the gateway has no usable credential for the account) or `service_unavailable`.

post.summary: Accept Bedrock models' AWS Marketplace agreements
post.description: Permission `catalog_write` (owner, admin; org-wide only). Accepting creates AWS Marketplace subscriptions in the tenant's AWS account, billed per use at the offer's rates. Name each model with the offer id it was seen with (`models`, at most 100); there is no server-side "all". Only an account connected with the organization's own role or key may accept: one the gateway calls with its process credential is refused (`agreements_need_tenant_credential`), since accepting would subscribe the operator's AWS account. Every named model's offers and agreement are read first: if any named offer is no longer current, nothing is accepted (`agreement_offer_changed`, with `changes`); if the role may read no named model's offers, nothing is accepted (`agreement_permission_missing`); both refusals are audited (`model_agreement.accept`, failed). A model whose offers alone could not be read fails with that reason. The gateway never makes a billed call to accept terms. Each model to accept is recorded first (an attempt in `accepting` state, audited `model_agreement.accepting`) and committed, then accepted with `CreateFoundationModelAgreement`, unless Bedrock already has an agreement (available or pending), which is `already_accepted`. A `ConflictException` is also taken as `already_accepted`: AWS does not document it, so this is an assumption, and the worker's availability check marks it failed if no agreement appears. A model AWS did not answer for in time is `unconfirmed`; an attempt whose request died is settled by the worker from availability (accepted when available or pending, else failed `acceptance_interrupted` after 5 minutes). Results are per model; one model's failure does not undo another's acceptance. Each result is audited (`model_agreement.accepted`, `model_agreement.already_accepted`, `model_agreement.failed`, with the actor; the event names the acceptance attempt, which keeps the account, model, offer id, the rate card shown, the outcome and AWS's error type), and the request as `model_agreement.accept`. The worker then checks each agreement with the free `GetFoundationModelAvailability` every 20 seconds for up to 30 minutes: `pending`, then `available` (its identifiers are recorded as entitled evidence and a discovery run is queued), or `failed`. Without `verify` the gateway sends no model request at acceptance. But if automatic offers are on for the account, that discovery run verifies each identifier it would offer with one 1-token request (billed by AWS, at most hourly per identifier) before offering it; with automatic offers off, nothing calls the model until someone routes to it. With `verify`, each foundation model is called once (a 1-token request) and that identifier is not probed again by discovery: `verified`, or `refused` with `access_request_required` when AWS still refuses the model for the account, which only a request to AWS changes. Requires `Idempotency-Key`; a replay returns the recorded results without calling AWS. D-035.

parameters.name: adapter_instance_key
parameters.description: The Bedrock provider account's adapter instance key.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key. A retry with the same key and request replays the stored outcome; a different request under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`.

200.description: Per-model results, or an idempotent replay.

409.description: `agreement_offer_changed` (a named offer is no longer current; `changes` lists each model's current offers; nothing was accepted), `idempotency_conflict`, or `idempotency_in_progress`.

422.description: `invalid_agreement_request` (invalid key or body), `unknown_provider_account` (not declared by the active release), `agreements_unsupported` (the account is not Bedrock's), `agreements_need_tenant_credential` (the account is called with the gateway's process credential, not the organization's own: connect the account's role first), `agreement_permission_missing` (the connection's role may not read offers or make agreements: grant the optional *accept model agreements* permissions; nothing was accepted), or `request_body_unprocessable`.

agentToken.description: An agent token (`Authorization: Bearer gwa_…`), for automation: it acts as its agent, only in the agent's organization, with the agent's role. Created with `POST /api/admin/v1/organizations/{org}/agents/{agent_id}/tokens` or, on the server, `gateway agent create`.

Forbidden.description: `forbidden`: the actor lacks the required permission for the organization.

NotFound.description: `not_found`: the named release does not exist in the organization.

Operation.description: A catalog operation. Streaming is a delivery mode of chat: a streamed request uses the alias's `chat` route, price and limits. `chat_stream` appears only in releases stored before that change, which keep routing as they did. A manifest may still name it: an entry matching its `chat` counterpart is dropped, one without a counterpart becomes `chat`, and one that differs is refused (`invalid_manifest`). `chat_batch` and `embeddings_batch` are the batch operations (D-021): each has its own capability, price (the provider's batch price) and routes, and only provider families that run batch jobs accept them: OpenAI and Azure OpenAI (chat and embeddings), and Anthropic, Bedrock and Gemini (chat only), Bedrock and Gemini with a batch staging bucket and Gemini on Agent Platform only; a manifest declaring one for another family is refused (`invalid_manifest`). Lines no batch route takes run emulated at the on-demand price where the organization allows it. A batch route needs a batch price of its own.

digest.description: Hex SHA-256 of the canonical manifest.

reasoning_allowance_tokens.description: Reasoning tokens reserved beyond each request's output cap, for a model whose reasoning the cap does not bound (xAI's Grok reports reasoning apart from `completion_tokens` and reasons past `max_tokens`); 0 means reasoning falls within the cap. Set in the release manifest's capability (`reasoning_allowance_tokens`, omitted when 0); chat operations only. Reserved at the reasoning price (the output price when none is published).

tools.description: Whether the deployment takes function tools for this operation (D-032). Set in the release manifest's capability (`tools`, omitted when false); chat operations only. A route takes tools only when every deployment it routes to does; a request with tools to one that does not is refused with `tools_unsupported`. Automatic offers set it for Claude; set it for others whose provider documents tool calling for the model.

input_minor_per_token.description: Input price, in money units of `currency` per token; one unit is 10⁻⁶ of the currency's smallest unit (micro-cents for USD), so $2.50 per million tokens is `250`.

output_minor_per_token.description: Output price, in money units of `currency` per token; one unit is 10⁻⁶ of the currency's smallest unit (micro-cents for USD), so $2.50 per million tokens is `250`.

cached_input_minor_per_token.description: Cached input price, in money units of `currency` per token; one unit is 10⁻⁶ of the currency's smallest unit (micro-cents for USD), so $2.50 per million tokens is `250`.

reasoning_minor_per_token.description: Reasoning price, in money units of `currency` per token; one unit is 10⁻⁶ of the currency's smallest unit (micro-cents for USD), so $2.50 per million tokens is `250`.

other_minor_per_token.description: Other price, in money units of `currency` per token; one unit is 10⁻⁶ of the currency's smallest unit (micro-cents for USD), so $2.50 per million tokens is `250`.

DeploymentOperation.description: Capability and price are catalogued separately; either may be null. A route requires both.

weight.description: This deployment's share of its priority's traffic, relative to the alias's other deployments of the operation at that priority (D-023). 1 for a route of one deployment.

priority.description: Lower is preferred: a request goes to the lowest priority that has a healthy deployment.

activation_version.description: Version of the organization activation pointer, read before the releases: send `"v{activation_version}"` as `If-Match` when activating (`"v0"` before the first activation). An activation since then fails with `version_conflict` instead of being overwritten.

release_id.description: Resolved release; null only when none was named and none is active.
Resolved release; null only when none was named and none is active.
Resolved release; null only when none was named and none is active.

CatalogManifest.description: Catalog manifest (the same document `gateway catalog apply` reads): `release`, `providers`, `deployments`, `prices`, `routes`. At most 1 MiB. Validated and canonicalized server-side; its SHA-256 digest identifies the release. Each `routes` entry is `{alias, operation, deployment}` with optional `weight` (1–1000) and `priority` (1–10), both 1 when omitted; an alias may route one operation to up to 8 deployments, all priced in one currency (D-023).

activation_version.description: Version of the organization activation pointer; also returned as `ETag`.

ProviderSecretInput.description: `api_key` for every family except `bedrock`. Bedrock takes either `access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, and an optional `session_token`, or a `role_arn` that the gateway assumes with its own AWS identity through STS for short-lived credentials. `azure-openai` and `azure-ai-foundry` take either `api_key` or a Microsoft Entra `tenant_id` (with optional `client_id`, `endpoint` and `resource_id`) that the gateway signs in to with its own Entra identity for short-lived tokens; it is used once the gateway's operator binds the directory to the organization. `gemini` takes either `api_key` or a Google `service_account` (with an optional `project_id` to bill) that the gateway impersonates with its own Google identity for short-lived tokens, calling Gemini on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI), since the Gemini API no longer admits new service accounts; it is used once the gateway's operator binds the account to the organization. Keys are 1-8192 bytes without whitespace or control characters. Never echoed.

role_arn.description: IAM role in the tenant's account. Its trust policy must allow the gateway's AWS principal.

tenant_id.description: Directory (tenant) ID of the tenant's Microsoft Entra directory. Azure families only.

client_id.description: Application (client) ID of an app in the tenant's directory whose federated identity credential trusts the gateway. Without it, the gateway signs in as its own multi-tenant app. Only with `tenant_id`.

endpoint.description: The tenant's Azure resource: `https://<resource>.openai.azure.com` or `https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com` for `azure-openai`; `https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com` or `https://<resource>.cognitiveservices.azure.com` for `azure-ai-foundry`; or the same hosts in Azure Government (`.azure.us`) or Azure operated by 21Vianet (`.azure.cn`). Defaults to the gateway's configured endpoint; with it, no Azure adapter need be configured. Only with `tenant_id`. For `openai-compatible`: the tenant's own endpoint's base URL (`http` or `https`, no credentials, query or fragment; request paths such as `chat/completions` are joined to it, so it usually ends in `/v1`), with an optional `api_key` sent as a bearer token. The gateway reaches it over HTTPS at public addresses only, or at any address for an origin the operator allows (`GATEWAY_OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS`), checked and pinned on every connection.

resource_id.description: The same resource's Azure Resource Manager ID, `/subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/<group>/providers/Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/<name>`. With it, discovery lists the resource's deployments from Resource Manager (each deployment that can serve requests, the model and version it serves, and its operations), which needs the `Reader` role on the resource for the gateway's identity; without it, discovery of the account is unsupported. It must name the account `endpoint` (or the gateway's configured endpoint) calls: discovery checks the account's custom subdomain and lists nothing on a mismatch (`ResourceMismatch`). Only with `tenant_id`.

service_account.description: A service account in the tenant's Google Cloud project, `<name>@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, on which the gateway's Google identity holds `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator`. Gemini only.

project_id.description: The Google Cloud project where Agent Platform serves Gemini, and which it bills; defaults to the service account's own project, and is required for a default service account. Only with `service_account`.

location.description: The Agent Platform location: `global` or a region such as `us-central1`; defaults to the gateway's configured location, else `global`. Only with `service_account`.

ProviderCredential.description: Credential metadata. Secret material is never returned.

key_id.description: Identifies the encryption key that sealed the secret.

cloud_principal.description: Present only for a credential that has the gateway act as a tenant's cloud principal (an Entra directory, a Google service account): whether the gateway's operator has bound that principal to the organization. A `pending` credential is not used; ask the operator to bind it (`gateway cloud-principal allow`).

deployment.description: Deployment name, matched exactly in every release.

input_minor_per_token.description: Input price, in money units of `currency` per token; one unit is 10⁻⁶ of the currency's smallest unit (micro-cents for USD), so $2.50 per million tokens is `250`.

output_minor_per_token.description: Output price, in money units of `currency` per token; one unit is 10⁻⁶ of the currency's smallest unit (micro-cents for USD), so $2.50 per million tokens is `250`.

reason.description: Why; leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed.

effective_from.description: Defaults to now; a time in the past also starts now.

effective_until.description: Exclusive end; open-ended when absent. Must be later than the start.

input_minor_per_token.description: Input price, in money units of `currency` per token; one unit is 10⁻⁶ of the currency's smallest unit (micro-cents for USD), so $2.50 per million tokens is `250`.

other_minor_per_token.description: Other price, in money units of `currency` per token; one unit is 10⁻⁶ of the currency's smallest unit (micro-cents for USD), so $2.50 per million tokens is `250`.

price_version.description: Price version recorded on reservations priced by this override.

status.description: Status when the response was produced. A replayed response keeps the original status.

created_by.description: Null once the creating user is deleted.

status.description: `unsupported`: the provider family cannot list models.

attempts.description: Claims by the worker; a worker that stops mid-run is retried up to three attempts.

error_code.description: Fixed code for a failed or unsupported job, never provider text: `not_configured` (no credential serves the account), `attempts_exhausted`, or a provider error category such as `authentication`, `rate_limited`, `timeout`, or `protocol`.

models_listed.description: Models the listing reported; set when `succeeded`.

models_added.description: Models reported for the first time.

models_missing.description: Previously reported models this listing omitted.

requested_by.description: User who requested a manual job.

model.description: Provider model id, at most 255 bytes.

missing_since.description: When a successful listing first omitted the model; null while listed.

deployed.description: Whether a deployment of the active release names the model on this provider account.

operations.description: What the latest listing says the model supports: recorded only where the listing states it or the model's family makes it certain (Gemini on Agent Platform: `gemini-<version>-<pro|flash|flash-lite>` chats, streamed or not; `gemini-embedding-*`, `text-embedding-*` and `text-multilingual-embedding-*` embed). Null when unknown. Informational: routing uses the catalog's capabilities only.

availability.description: `listed`: the account's own listing reports the model where the gateway calls it. `unknown`: the listing is a catalog wider than that (Google's publisher models on Agent Platform cover every location), so the model may not be offered in the account's location; drift then compares deployments with Google's catalog, and a deployment of a model the location lacks is not reported as unlisted. `profile_only`: the account's listing reports the model, but only an inference profile can call it (a Bedrock foundation model whose inference types lack `ON_DEMAND`); automatic offers never offer its own identifier, only its profiles (`us.…`, `global.…`), which are priced by its name. `endpoint_only`: one of the account's own Agent Platform endpoints in its project and location (a model it deployed to dedicated machines, such as a Model Garden deployment or a tuned model), listed as `endpoints/<id>` with its display name and, in `deployment`, the deployed model taking most of its traffic: `model` and `version`, the machines in `sku` (`g2-standard-12 + 1 NVIDIA_L4`) and the minimum replica count in `capacity`. An endpoint whose deployed models the gateway recognizes (every one taking traffic a Gemini model, or a Model Garden container serving OpenAI chat completions) is `listed` instead, with operation `chat` and its wire API in `deployment.format`, and is called as `endpoints/<id>`; one whose deployed models it does not recognize stays `endpoint_only`, never offered or probed.

evidence.description: What the gateway has seen calling the model on this account; null when nothing yet.

deployment.description: Where the listing is the account's own deployments (Azure) or endpoints (Google), what this deployment serves and on what terms; null for listings of models. On Google's Agent Platform, `format` is the wire API the gateway calls the model with: `gemini`, `anthropic_messages` (Claude, through `rawPredict`), `mistral_chat` (Mistral, through `rawPredict`) or `openai_chat` (OpenAI chat completions: Agent Platform's `endpoints/openapi` for xAI and other partners, or the endpoint's own), for partner models (`<publisher>/<model>`) and endpoints alike. Shown to operators only: routing derives the wire API itself, and offers do not read it.

last_synced_at.description: When the latest successful listing finished.

unlisted_deployments.description: Deployments whose model the account no longer lists or never listed.

missing_since.description: When the account stopped listing the model; null if it never did.

source_version.description: Version the source states, e.g. a price sheet's `version`, as of the latest fetch. A new version label alone does not start a new snapshot.

fetched_at.description: When a fetch first saw these prices.

confirmed_at.description: The latest fetch that saw them unchanged.

unmapped.description: Published prices not recorded against a model: public price lists price products rather than models, so all of theirs are unmapped. A price mapping selects which one a deployment is compared with.

last_success_at.description: When the latest successful fetch finished.

last_error_code.description: Why the latest fetch failed; null after a success. Never provider text.

snapshot.description: The prices the source currently publishes; null until a fetch succeeds.

price_source.description: Whether the billed price is the release's or an effective price override's.

comparisons.description: One per source of the provider family with a snapshot; empty when there is none.

status.description: `matches`: every published, billable dimension equals the catalog price, or, for a published price finer than one money unit per token, the catalog price is it rounded up to the next unit (as adopting it bills). `differs`: at least one does not. `no_observation`: the source has no price for the mapped item or the model in the region compared. `currency_mismatch`: the source prices the model only in other currencies (`observed_currencies`). `not_comparable`: the currency's minor-unit exponent is unknown (e.g. internal credits), so money units cannot be derived. `unpublished`: the source publishes no billable dimension.

matched_by.description: `mapping`: an organization price mapping chose the published item. `model`: the published model name equals the deployment's model. `listing_name`: at the AWS Price List, for a Bedrock deployment without a mapping whose model the list does not name, the item named after the name the account's listing gives the model (`Claude Sonnet 4.6`, with ` · global` for a global inference profile), as automatic offers price it; each dimension is compared at the higher of that item's standard and long-context prices.

observed_item.description: The published item compared; null when no price in the catalog's currency was found.

observed_region.description: Region of the compared price; null for a global price or no match.

observed_currencies.description: With `currency_mismatch`, the currencies the source prices the model in; otherwise empty.

per_tokens.description: How many tokens the compared published prices are for; null when no price in the catalog's currency was found.

dimensions.description: Empty unless a price in the catalog's currency was compared.

catalog.description: Money units per token the catalog bills (10⁻⁶ of the currency's smallest unit).

observed.description: Published price in money units per token, exact. A fraction means the published price is finer than one money unit.

oneOf.description: Published decimal price in the currency's major unit, canonical: no leading or trailing zeros.

published.description: The decimal as published, per the observation's token count.

status.description: `matches`: the catalog price equals the observed one, or is it rounded up to a whole money unit where the observed price is finer. `unpublished`: the source states no price for this dimension. `not_reported`: the provider family never reports usage in this dimension, so it cannot be billed and is not drift.

item.description: The source's name for what it prices; what a price mapping names. Stable across fetches.

model.description: The model the price is recorded against; null for public price lists, whose items are products rather than models.

per_tokens.description: How many tokens the prices are for; public price lists are restated per million, exactly.

input.description: Published decimal price in the currency's major unit, canonical; null when not published.

output.description: Published decimal price in the currency's major unit, canonical; null when not published.

cached_input.description: Published decimal price in the currency's major unit, canonical; null when not published.

reasoning.description: Published decimal price in the currency's major unit, canonical; null when not published.

other.description: Published decimal price in the currency's major unit, canonical; null when not published.

item.description: The source's item, as the observation listing shows it. It need not be published now; drift then reports `no_observation`.

region.description: Compare with the item's price in this region. Absent or null prefers the deployment's `location`, then the global price.

aws_external_id.description: `qucelerate-<organization id>`: the `sts:ExternalId` the gateway presents when it assumes the organization's AWS roles.

aws_role_session_name.description: The session name of roles the gateway assumes for the organization, as CloudTrail shows it.

location.description: The location offered deployments declare, which also picks regional prices (a Bedrock account's AWS region). Absent or null takes the account's existing deployments' location.

applied_release_id.description: The release active after the latest successful run.

error_code.description: Why the latest run changed nothing: `no_active_release`, `account_not_declared`, `invalid_release` or `incompatible_price_override`.

deployment.description: The deployment it is, or would be, offered as; a price mapping may name it before it is offered.

status.description: `offered`: in the active release. `needs_price`: no source prices it; map its deployment to a published item. `unsupported`: not a chat or embedding model the adapter can call, or the listing cannot say the account may call it. `withdrawn`: an admin's release dropped it. `catalog_full`: the release has no room for it. `refused`: the account's evidence refuses the model (a call was refused for it, see `DiscoveredModel.evidence`); it is not offered, and an offered deployment is removed, until evidence verifies it again. `requires_action`: a read-only check during discovery found something the tenant must do first (`DiscoveredModel.evidence.reason`, such as `agreement_required`); it is not offered, and an offered deployment is removed, until a check or a call shows the account may call it. `unchecked`: the listing could not check whether the account may call the model where a first call could subscribe it (Bedrock's Marketplace models; D-035), and no evidence says it may; it is not offered until a listing checks it, and one already offered stays offered.

ModelEvidence.description: What the gateway itself has seen about whether this account can call the model (D-018), the latest observation. Recorded from inference traffic: a call that succeeds verifies the model; one the provider refuses for the model (403 access denied, 404 not found) refuses it. Throttling, outages, rejected requests and bad credentials record nothing. A process writes an unchanged verdict at most every ten minutes, so `observed_at` may lag the latest request by that much.

state.description: `verified`: a call succeeded. `refused`: a call was refused for the model (`reason`). `entitled`: a read-only control-plane check during discovery found the identity the gateway calls with holds the permission to call it (Azure: the inference role on the resource). `requires_action`: the check found something the tenant must do (`reason`). A control-plane check never replaces `verified` or `refused`: what a call showed is stronger.

reason.description: Why the model is refused: `access_denied` (403: the account or the gateway's identity may not call it, such as Bedrock's model access denials) or `not_found` (404: not served where the gateway calls it, such as a model retired for the account, absent in the location, or a deleted deployment); `permission_missing` (`requires_action`: the gateway's identity lacks the permission to call it, such as Azure's *Cognitive Services User* role on the resource, or Bedrock's IAM authorization); `agreement_required` (`requires_action`: the account has not accepted the model's offer terms, such as its AWS Marketplace agreement on Bedrock); `not_entitled` (`requires_action`: the provider restricts the model for the account, which the tenant lifts with the provider); `quota_zero` (`requires_action`: the project's request quota for the model is zero, such as a partner model on Google's Agent Platform, so every call is refused until the tenant has it raised); `policy_denied` (`requires_action`: an organization policy forbids the account to call the model, such as the Google project's effective `vertexai.allowedModels` policy, which the tenant's policy administrator changes); `enable_in_model_garden` (`requires_action`: the Google project has not enabled the Model Garden partner model, whose terms a project owner accepts on its Model Garden card). Null unless `state` is `refused` or `requires_action`.

deployment.description: The deployment the observation was made through.

provider_status.description: The provider's HTTP status for a refusal.

provider_code.description: The provider's error type for a refusal (`AccessDeniedException`, `NOT_FOUND`), never its message.

verified_at.description: The last time a call succeeded, kept when the model has since been refused.

DiscoveredDeployment.description: A listed deployment's details as the provider reports them; each is null when not reported or unusable.

format.description: The model's format, which says which API serves it (Azure: `OpenAI`, `Anthropic`, `xAI`, ...).

model.description: The model the deployment serves, which can differ from the deployment's name.

sku.description: The deployment type or SKU (Azure: `GlobalStandard`, `DataZoneStandard`, `ProvisionedManaged`, ...; a Google endpoint: its machines, `g2-standard-12 + 1 NVIDIA_L4`).

capacity.description: The capacity bought, in the SKU's unit (Azure: thousands of tokens per minute for standard deployment types, provisioned throughput units for provisioned ones; a Google endpoint: its minimum replica count).

content_filter.description: The content filter policy the deployment applies, as the cloud reports it (Azure's `raiPolicyName`).

format.description: The model's format, which says which API serves it (Azure: `OpenAI`, `Anthropic`, `xAI`, ...).

model.description: The model's name, as a deployment of it reports it.

lifecycle_status.description: The provider's lifecycle status (Azure: `GenerallyAvailable`, `Preview`, `Deprecating`, `Legacy`, `Deprecated`); null when not reported.

default_version.description: Whether a new deployment of the model gets this version by default.

skus.description: The deployment types (SKUs) it can be deployed with (Azure: `GlobalStandard`, `DataZoneStandard`, `ProvisionedManaged`, ...).

max_capacity.description: The most capacity one deployment may have, in its SKU's unit.

retires_at.description: When inference on this version retires; null when not reported.

operations.description: What the catalog says the model supports (chat completion: chat, streamed or not; embeddings); null when it states neither.

deployments.description: Names of the account's listed deployments (discovered models not missing) serving this format, model and version. Empty: none does, so using it needs a deployment.

listed_at.description: When the latest listing reported it.

auto_adopt.description: Whether published prices that differ are adopted automatically.

providers.description: Provider families requests may be sent to, sorted; `null` for any.

locations.description: Deployment locations (`location` in the manifest, matched exactly) requests may be sent to, sorted; `null` for any. A deployment without a location is not permitted while this is set.

catalog.description: Money units per token the catalog bills.

observed.description: Published money units per token, exact; a fraction where finer than one unit.

proposed.description: What adopting it would bill: `observed` rounded up to a whole unit.

source.description: The source whose price is held; for disagreeing sources, the first.

reason.description: `large_increase`: a dimension more than doubles. `large_decrease`: one falls below half. `to_zero`: a billed dimension becomes free. `sources_disagree`: two sources publish different prices, or one publishes the catalog's price and another a new one.

release_id.description: The active release it was found against.

ContentFilterPolicy.description: A content filter policy as the cloud reports it (Azure's `raiPolicies`).

base_policy.description: The policy it is based on (`Microsoft.DefaultV2`).

system_policy.description: Whether the cloud reports it as its own default policy (`SystemManaged`) rather than one the account made.

dimension.description: Bedrock's rate dimension, prefixed with its region code (`USE2_input_tokens_global_standard`).

rate_card.description: The account's region's rates where the card names them (`rate_card_region`), else the card's first 100.

rate_card_region.description: The region code the card was narrowed to (`USE2` for us-east-2), or null for the whole card.

rate_card_total.description: How many rates the whole card has.

legal_url.description: The offer's legal terms (EULA): a link AWS signs, which expires.

status.description: `pending` (accepted; AWS has not reported it available), `available` (available per AWS; not called unless `probe`), `verified` (the probe succeeded), `refused` (the probe was refused, or AWS reports the account not entitled or the role not authorized to call the model, or the region not serving it: see `reason`; the model is recorded entitled only when the agreement, authorization, entitlement and region all allow it), `failed`.

probe.description: Whether a billed 1-token probe was asked for (`verify`).

checking.description: Whether the worker is still checking it.

model.description: The foundation model the agreement is for.

unblocks.description: Its listed identifiers (the model and its inference profiles) that need it.

deployments.description: The automatically offered deployments serving them.

agreement_required.description: Whether an identifier's evidence still says `agreement_required`.

offers.description: Read live, only for a model still needing an agreement.

permission.description: `granted` when offers could be read, `missing` when the role may not read them, `unknown` when nothing was read.

model.description: A foundation model identifier, as `GET` lists it.

offer_id.description: The offer it was seen with.

models.description: Each model to accept, with the offer id it was seen with. There is no "accept all": a client accepting every listed model sends each pair (a model with several offers needs one chosen).

verify.description: Once AWS reports an agreement available, call each foundation model once (a 1-token request, billed by AWS); the identifier called counts as discovery's probe, so it is not probed again. Off by default: the gateway sends no model request at acceptance and the model is `available` per AWS, not yet called. But with automatic offers on for the account, the discovery run queued once it is available verifies each identifier it would offer with one 1-token request (at most hourly per identifier) before offering it; with them off, nothing calls the model until someone routes to it.

outcome.description: `accepted` (AWS made the agreement), `already_accepted` (AWS had one, or answered `ConflictException`, which the gateway takes to mean one exists; the worker's availability check corrects it if not), `unconfirmed` (AWS did not answer in time; the worker settles it from availability), `failed` (see `reason`; `not_attempted` when the request ran out of time before calling AWS for it).

status.description: `pending` for an agreement made or found; the worker moves it on (read it with `GET`).
